evidence: Caes. B.G. 6.38.2: in summō rem esse discrīmine (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a dividing line or interval; then the point that decides between two outcomes, a turning point, a crisis, a danger. Its common everyday sense is a difference (sine discrīmine, without distinction).

evidence: Caes. B.C. 1.54: cum in hīs angustiīs rēs esset (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Quinct. 5: in summās angustiās addūcī
terms.comment: Properly a narrow place, a pass; then any tight spot, and shortage of money (angustiae reī familiāris).
Especially in the plural, the times, of hard or dangerous circumstances (Lewis & Short): amīcōrum temporibus, to a friend’s difficulties (Cic. Fam. 10.1.2).

sources: Lewis & Short: discrimen · Lewis & Short: angustiae · Lewis & Short: tempus
